*See also: [How to do it](eportfolio-guide.qmd) · [Criteria](eportfolio-criteria.qmd) · [Checklist](eportfolio-checklist.qmd) ·
[Common mistakes](eportfolio-mistakes.qmd)*

The IB publishes example ePortfolios in its teacher support material. **Example 18** is a music performance portfolio
from an earlier unit, with a different statement of inquiry: *Art reflects interconnectedness across space and time*. Ours
is *Art questions power and privilege*, so read it for **how it is built**, not for what it says. Your teacher has the
full files; ask to see them.

The files come without marks or examiner comments, so we do not know what it scored. Take it as one way to build a
portfolio, not as a model answer.

## How the 30 pages are spent

| File | What it is | Size | Counts as |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task 1 | Investigation of soul music, critique of *Glory* (John Legend and Common, 2014) | 7 pages | 7 |
| Task 2 | Exploration and artistic intention, written | 8 pages | 8 |
| Task 2 | Process video | 2:44 | 5.5 |
| Task 3 | Performance video of *Stand Up* (Cynthia Erivo) | 2:57 | 6 |
| Task 4 | Evaluation and reflection | 3 pages | 3 |
| Bibliography | | 1 page | 0 |
| | | **Total** | **≈ 29.5 of 30** |

The student planned the length of every file. The performance is under 3 minutes because, they explain in Task 4, "the 3
minute time limit dictated that I could only perform a part of the song, so I chose the second verse onwards". Choosing a
portion and saying why is allowed, and it is the right way to handle a song that is too long.

## Task 1: what to notice

- **A genre, not an artist.** Ai is about soul as a whole: where it came from (R&B and gospel), the regional styles
  (Memphis, Detroit, Philadelphia), the key artists *as part of* the genre, and its characteristics.
- **Characteristics you can hear.** Call and response, backbeat and syncopation, vamping, the instruments of the band,
  seventh and ninth chords, vocal techniques (melisma, falsetto, runs). This is the "what it sounds like" that many
  portfolios leave thin.
- **A section on the statement of inquiry.** A whole heading ("Soul music reflects interconnectedness across space and
  time") argues the link instead of mentioning it once.
- **Aii starts with context.** Before the music, it sets out why *Glory* was written (the film *Selma*) and how it links
  1965 to 2014.
- **What to do better in your own:** check that your Aii has **techniques with time stamps** and a **judgement** of
  strengths *and* limitations, not only praise.

## Task 2: what to notice

- **Three ideas, weighed.** Before choosing, the student lays out three possible versions (with piano and DAW; a soul and
  hip-hop fusion; a cappella), each with its strengths and its risks, then merges two and says why.
- **Three stages.** The written journal is split into Stage 1, 2 and 3 of the song's development, and a **process video**
  carries the sound. The writing explains the clips; it does not replace them.
- **Choices tied to research.** The a cappella opening is justified by the history traced in Task 1 (the music of enslaved
  people in the fields, call and response from gospel).

## Task 3: what to notice

A video, not only audio, and the student says why in Task 4: a video captures the whole performance, voice and body. If
you film, make sure you can be seen and heard clearly; if audio serves your piece better, use audio.

## Task 4: what to notice

- **Di is organised by element.** Key, genre, dynamics, rhythm, structure, melody, instruments, texture, harmonies, DAW:
  each judged against the artistic intention.
- **Limitations are specific.** The backing track is too quiet at one point; one line is "slightly off the beat"; cutting
  the song lost some of its context.
- **Outside feedback.** The student asked peers and two musicians, and says what they learned from it.
- **Dii is about the musician.** It names skills that changed (the move between head voice and middle register, piano
  inversions, harmonies built in Logic Pro), what influenced them, and what they now listen to.
- **What to do better in your own:** point each skill in Dii to the **Task 2 clip** where it changed.
